Caveats recorded with the ranking

  • Open Targets association scores already include known-drug and literature evidence, so those components are not independent of ot_overall.
  • Ranking reflects weight of existing evidence, not causality.
  • Accessibility is a hard gate: failing targets score 0.

Experimental-complex gate

24 of 33 admitted

Gate: method in X-RAY DIFFRACTION, ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, ELECTRON CRYSTALLOGRAPHY, SOLUTION NMR, NEUTRON DIFFRACTION, resolution ≤ 4Å, target chain ≥ 40 residues, and at least one chain that is a known interaction partner. Antibody and Fab chains are classified separately: they show an epitope is targetable by a biologic, but blocking a defined interaction needs the native partner. A native-partner complex does not guarantee a reachable interface; stage 4 enforces the extracellular-span check on real residue numbers once interfaces are computed.

Existing binders for these targets

6 of 24 targets have a designed binder in the PDB

Every binder in this record is an existing molecule from the PDB or from clinical data. None was designed by this pipeline, which has produced no binder. Overlap with a selected epitope is evidence that the surface is bindable, not that a new binder against it would work.

None of these binders came from this pipeline. Every molecule below already exists — a designed binder deposited in the PDB, or a clinical antibody. They are shown because an existing binder against the same surface is evidence that the surface is bindable; that is not evidence that a new binder against it will have useful affinity or specificity.

Of the 3 published de novo binder(s) at mini-binder scale (≤ 100 residues) whose footprint could be mapped, 3 engage every hotspot this pipeline selected for that target. Larger designed scaffolds (DARPins and designed scFvs) in the table below mostly do not — they were raised against other surfaces. Read a zero there carefully: where the deposited construct does not even contain the selected epitope, the zero is silence about that surface rather than evidence against it, and the row says which case applies.

Calibrate that agreement honestly: these are the canonical ligand-binding interfaces of well-studied receptors, which is where both a human designer and this pipeline would look first. Convergence on them is a sanity check that the epitope selection is not eccentric — it is not evidence that the pipeline finds non-obvious sites, and it does not extend to the targets here that have no published designed binder.

Example complexes

CD274 — PD-L1 de novo binder

58 aa designed

Methods and parameters

Definitions

interface residue
heavy-atom contact within cutoff OR buried SASA >= min_delta_sasa
hotspot
interface residue in an extracellular span, making a contact, ranked by buried SASA
numbering
author numbering mapped to UniProt via SIFTS alignment; never assumed equal

Only the top 2 complexes per target were analysed, so this is not a complete epitope survey of the PDB.

Data sources

  • Open Targets Platform: associations (incl. literature and genetic_literature datatype scores), tractability, safety, genetic constraint, target class, baseline expression, interaction partners
  • UniProt: topology-based accessibility and extracellular spans
  • ChEMBL: mechanism and action-type precedent
  • ClinicalTrials.gov v2: clinical precedent including stopped trials
